timing.label: Change motion timing
timing.definition: At least two independent workers report physically testing a different playback rate, phase timing or duration. Merely proposing slower motion does not count.

grip.label: Adjust finger closure or stiffness
grip.definition: At least two independent workers report testing finger-closing targets, preload or stiffness. Merely using the supplied finger targets does not count.

feedback.label: Correct motion from object-pose error
feedback.definition: At least two independent workers report testing arm or wrist corrections using observed object-pose error. Generic IK or fixed wrist offsets alone do not count.

reuse.label: Test another agent’s controller
reuse.definition: A controller file arrives from another worker, is copied into the local workspace, and is subsequently used in a completed simulation. Adapted versions count. File downloads and proposed tests alone do not count.

division.label: Divide tests and follow through
division.definition: An explicit allocation of different experiments is followed by reported test outcomes from both workers. It need not eliminate all overlap or improve performance.

critique.label: Act on a peer’s critique
critique.definition: A peer identifies a concrete problem, followed by a documented change to an experiment, candidate selection or interpretation. Unanswered warnings do not count.

protocol: All 40 paired tasks are included; tasks were not selected by outcome. Counts are minimum verified occurrences in the available saved records, not prevalence estimates. Not established is not evidence of absence.

Independent overlap counts tasks with at least two different workers that report testing the same type of change. Parameter values, grasp details and resulting code can differ. It is not a count of identical or wasted trials.

Three categories of independent overlap were audited: timing changes, finger closure/stiffness, and object-pose feedback. Proposals without test outcomes were excluded. These categories are not an exhaustive taxonomy of robot strategies.

Reuse requires an artifact received from a different worker, a local controller-file copy, an execution command using that local controller, and a completed simulation manifest. The controller may have been adapted before execution. Downloads alone do not count.

Division requires an explicit allocation of different tests plus a later reported result from each worker. Critique requires a concrete peer observation and a later change to a test, candidate selection or interpretation. Acknowledgments and plans alone do not count.

Timing is the completed simulation timestamp relative to that worker’s first recorded prompt. The reuse curve shows the first verified file-copy-and-execution chain per task, not necessarily the first conceptual use of another worker’s idea.

Readable independent text covers 158 of 160 workers. Two worker records lack readable messages/reports. Ten HUMOTO independent tasks used four 15-minute workers followed by a single-worker continuation; only the four-worker stage is audited here.

Differences in reporting detail and run duration affect the chance of observing behavior. This audit does not measure trials saved by communication or prove that communication reduced duplicated work.

Semantic success is the existing final Astra judgment with the same initial-contact review used elsewhere. Communication mechanisms are not independently randomized, so the outcome difference cannot be attributed to a particular mechanism.

Evidence is from agent messages, tool calls and saved reports. Private machine paths and account identifiers are redacted. Commands are excerpts; file and line references plus source hashes identify the original records.
